chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Abu Al-Magra, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I go to the money-changer with dirhams and buy dinars from him, and he weighs for me more than my due right. Then I buy from him, in exchange for those dinars, dirhams.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it, but do not weigh less than your due right.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهَا بَأْسٌ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying gold with silver when the money-changer gives extra weight during the exchange?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of currency exchange (sarf) by distinguishing between the initial weighing and the final settlement, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding riba al-fadl. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits the money-changer to provide a slight excess during the initial weighing of dirams for dinars, provided the buyer does not give less than their due right in the subsequent transaction. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in commercial transactions while maintaining the core principle of fairness and avoiding exploitation in the exchange of like-for-like commodities.
